tagline: The whole squad, under the lights.
sector: Officially licensed collectible trading cards for a touring North American and European club football tournament, sold into grocery, newsstand and hobby channels through a national licensing partner.
founded_place_size: touring competition, Western Europe and North America; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
about: Continental Cup 2026 is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is touring competition, Western Europe and North America, and this commission covers phase 2: squad press run and partner files.
audience: Collectors aged sixteen to forty five who buy officially licensed sets beside other marquee cards, in grocery aisles, at newsstands and in hobby shops. They notice when a card in the pack looks like it came from somewhere else.
price_positioning: A flagship licensed pack retailing around fourteen dollars, positioned above community and league sets and below fine-art prints. It must read as a marquee cup collectible, saturated and cinematic, never as a cheap programme or a gallery piece.
typography: A heavy, near-metallic display face for the player name and squad number, set large and confident, paired with a clean condensed sans for the position, club line and set year. The type should feel like a stadium scoreboard, not a school sports day.
voice: Bold, terse, terrace-proud. Copy is short and declarative. Example line the brand would write: 'Eighteen players. One set. Every card earns its place in the sleeve.'
brand_assets_status: There is no surviving design file or logo artwork. The tournament mark now exists only on printed things: the sole reference is a handheld photograph of a pitch-side sponsor board carrying the mark in one deep ink on a pale board. It has to be recovered as usable artwork before it can be placed at any size.
values: A licensed set is a promise: every player is who the card says, and the look holds across the whole squad rather than favouring a hero. Consistency in the sleeve is the product.
